name: Piscis alata
note: A speculative field note written by Claude. The species is invented; the natural history of every part it is made from is real.
mythology: It learned to leap from the arowana, the dragon-fish that jumps out of the river to take insects from overhanging branches. One evening it leapt, caught a dragonfly, and instead of eating it kept its wings. The next evening it caught another, and another, until every fin it had was a dragonfly's wing. Now it cannot stay under the water for long, and it cannot stay out of it either. The fishermen on the flooded rivers say that when the light is low you can see it between the two, gliding just above the surface with its wings out.
lineage: Its fins are dragonfly and damselfly wings, a lineage about 300 million years old, older than any fish fin it replaced. Its swim bladder is an arowana, a 'bony-tongued' fish of a very old lineage. Its ribs include the tarpon and the bowfin, two fish that can gulp air at the surface, which may be why it survives out of the water as long as it does.
habitat: Flooded forests and slow blackwater rivers, where branches hang low over the water and insects gather at dusk.
behaviour: It hunts at dusk by leaping. Its eyes and vertebrae are water bears, so when the floods drain away it dries out in the mud, curled up, and waits for the rains to return it to the river.
